title: Finiteness of the n-fold relative Frobenius
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $S$ be a scheme of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], and let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an integer $n\geq1$, let $F_S^n:S\to S$ and $F_X^n:X\to X$ be the n-fold absolute $p$-power Frobenius maps [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Put $X^{(p^n/S)}=X\times_{S,F_S^n,S}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $F_{X/S}^{(n)}:X\to X^{(p^n/S)}$ be the unique morphism whose composites with the two projections are $F_X^n$ and $f$, respectively (the n-fold relative Frobenius). Then $F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CCD, label lemma-relative-frobenius-finite; Tag 0CCG, label remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius

proof.text: Put $Y_i=X\times_{S,F_S^i}S$ with projections $\pi_i:Y_i\to X$ and $s_i:Y_i\to S$; identify $Y_0$ with $X$, $\pi_0$ with the identity, and $s_0$ with $f$. Every $Y_i$ has characteristic $p$: the sheaf map of $s_i$ sends $p\cdot1=0$ to $p\cdot1$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. Here are the identifications needed for iteration, explicitly from [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $Z_i=Y_i\times_{S,F_S}S$ with projections $a_i:Z_i\to Y_i$ and $b_i:Z_i\to S$. The pair $(\pi_i a_i,b_i)$ gives a map $\theta_i:Z_i\to Y_{i+1}$ because $f\pi_i a_i=F_S^i s_i a_i=F_S^{i+1}b_i$. Conversely, the pair $(\pi_{i+1},F_Ss_{i+1})$ defines $c_i:Y_{i+1}\to Y_i$, and $(c_i,s_{i+1})$ defines $\eta_i:Y_{i+1}\to Z_i$. Indeed, $\pi_{i+1}\theta_i\eta_i=\pi_i c_i=\pi_{i+1}$ and $s_{i+1}\theta_i\eta_i=s_{i+1}$, so $\theta_i\eta_i=\mathrm{id}$. Also $\pi_i c_i\theta_i=\pi_i a_i$ and $s_i c_i\theta_i=F_S b_i=s_i a_i$, so $c_i\theta_i=a_i$; together with $b_i\eta_i\theta_i=b_i$, this gives $\eta_i\theta_i=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\theta_i$ is an isomorphism. Let $u_i:Y_i\to Z_i$ be the one-step relative Frobenius and set $r_i=\theta_i u_i:Y_i\to Y_{i+1}$. Its projections satisfy $\pi_{i+1}r_i=\pi_iF_{Y_i}$ and $s_{i+1}r_i=s_i$. Existence of $u_i$ follows from $s_iF_{Y_i}=F_Ss_i$: both structure-sheaf maps send a section $t$ to $(s_i^\sharp t)^p$ [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0CCG, remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius: successive Frobenius twists and the first factorization formula; the fibre-product identifications are written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism] with its base $X$ equal to $S$, its scheme $V$ equal to $Y_i$, and its morphism $v$ equal to $s_i$. Its integrality conclusion makes $u_i$ integral, without any finite-type or quasi-compactness assumption on $Y_i$. Hence $r_i$ is integral as well, directly by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: for every affine open $V\subseteq Y_{i+1}$, its inverse image $W=\theta_i^{-1}(V)$ is isomorphic to $V$, hence affine, and $r_i^{-1}(V)=u_i^{-1}(W)$ is affine. The section map $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(r_i^{-1}(V))$ is the composite of the isomorphism $\mathcal O(V)\cong\mathcal O(W)$ with the integral section map of $u_i$. For each element of the last ring, take its monic equation over $\mathcal O(W)$ and replace every coefficient by its inverse image in $\mathcal O(V)$; the resulting monic equation proves integrality. For $i\geq1$ set $C_i=r_{i-1}\circ\cdots\circ r_0:X\to Y_i$. The base case $C_1=r_0$ is integral. If $C_i$ is integral, clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] applied to $C_i$ and $r_i$ makes $C_{i+1}=r_iC_i$ integral. Thus $C_n$ is integral.

source.place: Tag 0CCB, lemma-relative-frobenius (integrality); Tag 0CCG, remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius; composition: morphisms.tex Tag 01WK, lemma-composition-finite, second sentence

proof.text: We identify $C_n$ with the morphism in the statement, rather than assuming the iteration formula of Tag 0CCG. For $i=1$, the projections of $C_1$ are $F_X$ and $f$ by step 1. If $\pi_iC_i=F_X^i$ and $s_iC_i=f$, then $\pi_{i+1}C_{i+1}=\pi_iF_{Y_i}C_i=F_X\pi_iC_i=F_X^{i+1}$ and $s_{i+1}C_{i+1}=s_iC_i=f$. The middle equality is naturality of absolute Frobenius: on sections it is the identity $\pi_i^\sharp(t^p)=(\pi_i^\sharp t)^p$, and on spaces Frobenius is the identity [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. By uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product], the two projection identities imply $C_n=F_{X/S}^{(n)}$. In particular $F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ is integral and $s_nF_{X/S}^{(n)}=f$.

source.place: Tag 0CCG, remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius, first factorization formula, proved by induction on both projections; naturality is lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity, Tag 0CC7

proof.text: The factorization $f=s_n\circ F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ has locally finite type composite by the hypothesis on $f$. Clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], applied to $F_{X/S}^{(n)}:X\to Y_n$ and $s_n:Y_n\to S$, therefore shows that $F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ is locally of finite type. This clause requires no separatedness, finite-type, or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $s_n$ or $S$.

source.place: Tag 01T8, lemma-permanence-finite-type; this packages the finite-type part of the affine argument in varieties.tex Tag 0CCD, lemma-relative-frobenius-finite

proof.text: The map $F_{X/S}^{(n)}$ is integral by steps 2 and 3 and locally of finite type by step 4. The reverse implication of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft] now proves that it is finite. This is the finite-type-plus-integrality criterion used in the proof of Tag 0CCD, applied after the explicit iteration check, and proves the asserted result for every $n\geq1$.
